question_text: A company needs to give an application running on Amazon EC2 read-only access to one S3 bucket. Which approach is the most secure?

options.text: Attach an IAM role with only s3:GetObject permission for the required bucket to the EC2 instance.
Store an IAM user access key in the application configuration file.
Make the bucket public and restrict access by object name.
Use the root user access keys in an environment variable.

explanation: An IAM role provides short-lived credentials without embedding secrets. Least-privilege bucket access limits the application to the required action and resource.

explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations over time. Managed rules can identify public S3 buckets and trigger remediation workflows.

question_text: A web application must remain available if one Availability Zone fails. Which design best meets this requirement?

options.text: Run instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer.
Run one large instance with a larger EBS volume.
Place all instances in one Availability Zone with frequent snapshots.
Use a single NAT gateway for all workloads.

explanation: Multi-AZ Auto Scaling with an Application Load Balancer removes dependence on a single Availability Zone and replaces unhealthy capacity.

question_text: An application writes orders to a database and must continue accepting requests during a regional service disruption. Which pattern is most appropriate?

options.text: Use DynamoDB global tables with application routing designed for multiple Regions.
Use one Multi-AZ RDS instance and wait for it to recover.
Store the orders on an EC2 instance store volume.
Use an S3 lifecycle rule to copy backups weekly.

explanation: DynamoDB global tables replicate data across selected Regions and support multi-Region application designs. Multi-AZ protects within a Region, not against a regional event.

question_text: Users upload large files directly to a web application. The application servers are becoming a bottleneck. What should the architect recommend?

options.text: Generate S3 presigned URLs so clients upload directly to Amazon S3.
Increase the web server instance size.
Send files through a NAT gateway before storing them.
Save all files in an Amazon EFS file system.

explanation: Presigned URLs let clients upload directly to S3 while retaining controlled, time-limited access. This removes file transfer work from the application tier.

question_text: A globally distributed audience experiences high latency when loading static assets from an S3 bucket. Which solution improves delivery performance?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as an origin.
Move the bucket to a larger EC2 instance.
Use an EBS volume attached to the web servers.
Send every request through AWS Site-to-Site VPN.

explanation: CloudFront caches static objects at edge locations close to viewers, reducing latency and origin load.

question_text: A development environment is used only during business hours and has predictable usage. Which option most directly reduces compute cost?

options.text: Schedule nonproduction EC2 instances to stop outside required hours.
Use larger On-Demand instances at all times.
Store application logs only in instance memory.
Move the workload to a single Availability Zone.

explanation: Stopping nonproduction instances when they are not needed avoids compute charges while retaining the ability to restart them.

question_text: A company retains data for several years. Data is accessed frequently for 30 days and rarely afterward, but must be retrievable when required. Which S3 approach is appropriate?

options.text: Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to a lower-cost storage class after 30 days.
Delete all objects after 30 days.
Keep all objects in S3 Standard indefinitely.
Copy objects manually to an EC2 instance.

explanation: Lifecycle policies automate transitions based on age and access requirements, reducing storage cost while preserving retrieval.

An Amazon S3 static website.

explanation: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a standby in another Availability Zone and performs managed failover for supported engine deployments.

question_text: An API receives unpredictable traffic bursts and tasks can be processed asynchronously. Which architecture scales efficiently?

options.text: Amazon API Gateway, Amazon SQS, and AWS Lambda consumers.
A fixed fleet of one EC2 instance.
A manual file transfer process.
A single EBS volume shared over the internet.

explanation: API Gateway accepts requests, SQS buffers bursts, and Lambda scales consumers based on queued work. This decouples ingestion from processing.

question_text: A batch workload is fault tolerant and can pause when capacity is unavailable. Which purchasing option is generally suited to this workload?

options.text: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances.
Dedicated Hosts only.
A permanently running On-Demand instance.
Provisioned IOPS for an unused volume.

explanation: Spot Instances can offer significant savings for interruption-tolerant workloads. Applications should checkpoint and handle interruptions.
